note.text: Manufacturing changes materials into new products or assembles components. A factory combines material, labour, energy and capital inputs through a process, then distributes outputs. Extraction supplies a material; it is not automatically manufacturing. Transport and retail provide services. A firm may combine these activities, so classify the operation described rather than its company name.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to classify an activity from its transformation of inputs into manufactured outputs. Builds on: Form Four economic activities. Leads to: industrial clusters and location.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: Manufacturing changes materials into new products or assembles components. A factory combines material, labour, energy and capital inputs through a process, then distributes outputs. Extraction supplies a material; it is not automatically manufacturing. Transport and retail provide services. A firm may combine these activities, so classify the operation described rather than its company name.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: In an invented Douala enterprise, timber is delivered to a workshop, cut and joined into tables, then carried to shops. Making the tables is manufacturing. Felling the trees is primary production; carrying tables is transport; selling them is retail. Waste and energy use also belong in the production account.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Name the input, describe the transformation, then name the output. Check whether the case instead extracts a resource or provides a service. Explain the process before choosing its sector.

pick.q: An invented firm washes, presses and packages fruit as juice. Which operation is manufacturing?
e: Growing fruit is primary production.
Carrying goods is a transport service.
Selling is distribution rather than processing.
pick.y: Fruit is transformed into a different marketable product.

pick.q: Ayuk assembles purchased components into radios. Which classification fits assembly?
e: No mineral is being extracted.
Assembly changes components into a product.
The activity makes radios rather than moving passengers.
pick.y: Manufacturing can assemble components without extracting their materials.

pick.q: Bih compares quarrying stone with making cement. Which operation transforms materials into a manufactured product?
e: Extraction obtains a raw material.
Transport moves an already made product.
Advertising supplies a service.
pick.y: The distinction concerns the operation, not whether both firms use machinery.

right.text: material input: a substance used to make a product.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: Materials enter the production process. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

right.text: manufacturing process: transformation or assembly that makes a product.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: The material is transformed into a manufactured output. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

right.explain: This distinction is correct: An output is the result of the specified manufacturing process. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.
